# On-screen elements (DOM HUD + in-canvas overlays), input, audio and output resolution in holtburger-web (HB = external/holtburger/apps/holtburger-web)
Every file:line below was read unless an item is marked otherwise. Paths are relative to HB.

(1) WHAT CAN APPEAR ON SCREEN. Four layers, with a different way to hide each one.
A) Page chrome: direct <body> children without an hb- id, in index.html:620-967. These are h1/p/h2, #results (the smoke-check text), #login-form (which includes the #render-scale select), #login-status, #selection (#character-ul, plus #post-spawn holding the legacy #chat-panel / #vitals-panel / #inventory-panel), #create-*, #render-status and #stage. #stage contains #canvas-column (#fullscreen-btn :937, #canvas :938, #virtual-keypad :945) and #stage-info :965. Agent-mode hides all of this. ?hud=none on its own does NOT: it hides only body>*:not(#stage), so #fullscreen-btn, the keypad and #stage-info stay visible, and the canvas keeps its non-agent size of min(innerW-32,1920) x min(innerH-320,1080).
B) HUD DOM: direct body children whose id starts with hb-, or that carry .hb-bar / .hb-pill / .hb-panel.
 - Toolbar .hb-bar (ui/bar.js:648; mounted on document.body at app/plugin_bar.js:645).
 - Vitals orbs #hb-vitals-orb-hp/-stam/-mana plus #hb-vitals-orbs-defs (plugins/vitals-orbs.js:1004/1388).
 - #hb-radar (radar.js:651/708), #hb-buffs-hud (buffs-hud.js:1175/1222), #hb-chat-panel (chat-panel.js:420/567), #hb-status-indicators and #hb-portal-storm-pulse (status-indicators.js:464/440/671), #hb-hotbar (hotbar.js:764/1458), #hb-spell-strip (combat-bar.js:1141/1504).
 - #hb-combat-hud and the "You died." narrative #hb-combat-hud-death (combat-hud.js:533/914).
 - #hb-main-panel, #hb-hover-tooltip (hover-tooltip.js:140), #hb-radial-menu, #hb-examine-floaty, #hb-corpse-loot-bar, #hb-vendor-bar, #hb-modal-dialog.
 - Spew-box / rejection toasts #hb-rejection-toast-N (plugins/rejection_feedback.js:295-299). Each lasts 5 s, at most 4 at once. Transient lines, including server replies to teleports, land here.
 - #hb-jump-charge (index.html:5498-5503; only while Space is held).
 - #hb-portal-space-notice, which reads "In Portal Space - Please Wait..." (scene3d/portal_space.js:1028-1036).
 - #hb-thought-overlay (rynth/ai/thought_overlay.js:50; only with ?thoughtOverlay=1 and the rynth AI director running).
 - #hb-charselect (only with autoSpawn=select or a manual Connect).
 Agent-mode leaves ALL of these visible. ?hud=none hides them with CSS only: the plugins still install and tick. ?plugins=none skips bar/HUD mounting entirely (index.html:1914-1929), and window.__pluginClient is still created (index.html:4660-4662). The disconnect banner #hbDisconnectBanner (app/dom_utils.js:21-29) has no hyphen in its id, so both agent-mode and hud=none hide it.
C) DOM overlays inside #canvas-column:
 - #selection-brackets-3d (scene3d/selection_brackets.js:1099-1119, z-index 11). ON by default. Agent-mode explicitly re-shows it (index.html:525, display:block !important). It is not constructed under ?hud=none or ?selectionIndicator=none (scene3d/index.js:3245-3262). At runtime, layer.setDisplayOn(false) (:898) hides it and stays hidden, because the CharacterOption 0x0E poll only re-applies on a change (:910-920).
 - #nameplate-layer-3d (scene3d/hud.js:372-399). OFF by default; enabled with ?nameplateDom=on (scene3d/index.js:3213-3233).
D) Inside the canvas (three.js; no CSS reaches these):
 - Speech/emote bubbles: a THREE.Sprite on inst.root, 4.5 s hold then 1.2 s fade (scene3d/speech_bubble.js:171-235). ALWAYS ON with no flag. Driven by kind=55 OVERHEAD_SPEECH (app/client_events.js:1568-1593) through EntityManager.showSpeechBubble (scene3d/entities.js:7154).
 - Nameplate sprites and buff badges: OFF by default; ?nameplates=on enables them and ?hud=none forces them off (nameplate_sprite.js:311-320, 747-748, 1007-1008).
 - Spell-shape preview (?spellShapePreview=on, spell_shape_preview.js:88) and cast-range ring (?castRangeRing=on, :742): both off by default.
 - The legacy selection torus appears only with ?selectionIndicator=ring|both. The ?selectionFlash=on click blink is off by default.
 - The portal tunnel replaces the entire world frame (scene3d/index.js:2738-2743; portal_space.js:1734-1780), followed by a black fade-in quad (portal_space.js:1783; called at scene3d/index.js:2783 and :2965).
 - A permanent orange 2 m "hello-cube" sits at AC world (0,0,5) (scene3d/index.js:1598-1606; liveScene3d.helloCube). It is only visible near landblock 0x0000.
 - The local player's own rig. If the player avatar is the camera operator, it will be in shot.
 No FPS, stall or perf DOM overlay exists. stall_probe, diag and latency_diag only write to the console or window objects, and plugins/debug-overlay.js is orphaned: it is not listed in plugins/index.json.

(2) ?agent=1 AS A CLEAN-FRAME BASE. index.html:604-619 adds the agent-mode class when ?agent=1 OR ?autoLogin=1, and the no-hud class when ?hud=none. The kill rule is at index.html:484, verbatim:
`html.agent-mode body > *:not(#stage):not([id^="hb-"]):not(.hb-bar):not(.hb-pill):not(.hb-panel) { display: none !important; }`
Supporting rules:
 - :456 body has margin 0, overflow hidden, black background.
 - :485-501 #stage is fixed at 100vw x 100vh; #stage>*:not(#canvas-column) and #canvas-column>*:not(#canvas) are hidden; #canvas is 100% !important.
 - :507-516 hides legacy ids (#plugin-bar, #chat-panel, #inventory-panel, #spellbook-panel, #combat-bar, #vitals-hud, #nameplate-layer-3d, #post-spawn, .floating-panel).
 - :525 re-shows #selection-brackets-3d.
What it leaves visible: every hb-* HUD in section B (the comment at :473-483 says this is intentional, so a person can play from the 1070 desktop shortcut), the brackets, all in-canvas items in D, and the 1px #ccc border on the canvas. That border comes from `#stage canvas { border:1px solid #ccc; image-rendering:pixelated; cursor:grab }` at :160; the agent #canvas rule at :497-501 never resets it, so it should show on the top and left edges in compositor screenshots (not in captureStream) — reasoned from the CSS, not observed.
Verdict: agent-mode alone is not a clean film frame. The minimum is ?agent=1&hud=none at load time. This matters because the canvas-sizing decision _isAgentMode is latched once in preInit3D (scene3d/index.js:881-887) and reused by the resize handler (:1872-1873), so adding the class later does not resize the canvas. On top of that, film mode needs runtime CSS for the border, cursor and pixelated scaling, and must suppress speech bubbles, clear the selection, and handle the local player rig.

(3) TELEPORTS. Every PlayerTeleport, including @teleloc, @tele and @telepoi, raises kind=33 PORTAL_SPACE_ENTERED (app/client_events.js:873-940). That emits 'portalSpaceEntered' on window.__pluginClient.events, then startPortalSpace(window.liveScene3d, {enterDid, loopDid, onExit}), which is DEFAULT ON.
Retail tunnel state machine (portal_space.js:113-131 constants, sequencer :473-594):
 - TUNNEL (state 3): the world is not drawn; the tunnel Setup 0x02000306 plays at 40 fps on black with a random camera roll.
 - The tunnel holds until kind=66 TELEPORT_ARRIVED (client_events.js:941-948 calls signalPortalArrived({cellId})) AND the destination cells are resident. Readiness is destinationCellsReady (:601: EnvCell container for indoor cells, terrainBakedLbs for outdoor).
 - Failsafes: 6 s after arrival; up to 60 s while an indoor build is still in flight (?portalHoldBuild); 20 s with no arrival at all; plus up to 1.5 s of shader-warm hold.
 - CONTINUE (state 4): at least 2 s and at most 5 s, leaving inside an animation-frame window.
 - TUNNEL_FADEOUT (state 5): 1 s.
 - WORLD_FADEIN (state 6): 1 s black quad.
 Total is arrival plus load plus about 4-7 s. While the tunnel owns the frame, the render loop is paced to 30 fps (?portalSpaceFps, scene3d/index.js:2413).
Sounds: an enter whoosh (UI SoundType 0x6A), a drone (?portalDrone), and an exit whoosh (0x6B) at the start of the fade-in. The exit whoosh has no URL override.
The notice DOM element is hb-* (see B).
Suppressing it: ?portalSpace=off. This is read from location.search on each kind=33 event (client_events.js:912-915), so history.replaceState can toggle it at runtime. endPortalSpace() (:1826) force-ends a running tunnel. The login tunnel is skipped for ?agent=1, but teleport tunnels are not (loginPortalSpaceSkipReason :191-205). With the tunnel off, the world stays drawn: the camera jumps immediately because camera.js:2664-2695 assigns the pose directly, and terrain/cells visibly pop in. The tunnel's background shader warm-up (?tunnelWorldWarm) also only runs while the tunnel owns the frame, so the first frames after arrival can hitch.
Readiness signals:
 - window.__portalSpace {state, arrived, arrivalCell, reason, t:{start, cells, ready, reveal, done}} (:1170-1199).
 - globalThis.__isPortalSpaceActive() (:1594), true from TUNNEL through WORLD_FADEIN.
 - Bus event 'portalSpaceExited' via onExit (client_events.js:934-936).
 - The exports destinationCellsReady and destinationBuildInFlight (:601/:617), and globalThis.__interiorBuildPending.
The recorder must pause during the tunnel window (cut around it), or run with portalSpace=off and gate on those readiness signals plus a frame-time settle.

(4) INPUT.
Keyboard: one funnel, ui/input-funnel.js (?inputFunnelV2, default ON). It is a single document capture-phase keydown/keyup pair (:635-711) behind one gate, injected at index.html:5409 as `() => enteredWorld && !isTypingInForm()`. Inside it:
 - Movement keystate (index.html:5633 and :5920, priority 100).
 - The camera keystate mirror and PageUp/PageDown zoom (camera.js:3154-3160).
 - The C camera-mode cycle follow > topDown > orbit (camera.js:3217-3221).
 - Picking's attack-abort and Escape handling (picking.js:2068-2071), the escape_action module, the hotbar, combat keys, spellbook, selection keys and emote keys.
 Raw edges reach wasm through handle.handleKeyAction (cmdInterp, default ON).
 window.__inputFunnel.poison("gate") blocks every gameplay keydown while keyups still clear state; unpoison() restores it. releaseHeld(reason) (:567) synthesizes keyups for all held keys except Space.
Outside the funnel:
 - F-key panel hotkeys: window keydown at app/plugin_bar.js:587.
 - Per-plugin Escape/Enter handlers.
 - Window blur handlers: index.html:6047-6093 (release movement, abort jump charge), camera.js:3142-3149 / 3168, and the funnel ledger at :701.
 - The virtual keypad, which fires synthetic KeyboardEvents (index.html:6242-6291).
Mouse (none of it goes through the funnel):
 - Follow-mode right-drag mouselook: canvas contextmenu/mousedown plus document mousemove/mouseup (camera.js:1067-1076). Pitch is clamped to [-0.5, 1.4] rad at :215-216, so a straight-down view is impossible in follow mode.
 - Wheel zoom (topDown, and follow only under the retailCamZoom flag) on the canvas (camera.js:3174-3192).
 - OrbitControls on the canvas in orbit mode (camera.js:1105).
 - Picking: click selects, double-click Uses (which can walk the player into a portal), drag-drop gives items, plus pointermove hover (picking.js:1451/1474/1488).
 - Hover tooltip: canvas mousemove plus window mousedown/keydown capture (plugins/hover-tooltip.js:266-270).
 - Input funnel: document capture mousedown and contextmenu suppression (:673-684).
There is no pointer lock anywhere; only stale comments mention it. Touch input exists only via OrbitControls and the keypad.
Recommended lock: releaseHeld("film") then poison("gate"), plus a window capture-phase blocker that calls stopImmediatePropagation and preventDefault on keydown, keyup, keypress, pointer*, mouse*, click, dblclick, auxclick, contextmenu, wheel (passive:false), touch*, dragstart and drop. A window capture listener runs before the document-capture funnel and before every element listener; only window-capture listeners registered earlier still run, and those are benign. Also call cameraSwitcher._endFollowDrag?.() and zero cameraSwitcher.keys. To restore, remove the blockers and call unpoison(). A DOM "shield" div is not viable: under agent-mode plus no-hud, any new body child or #stage/#canvas-column child is display:none !important.

(5) CURSOR, FOCUS AND RESOLUTION.
Cursor: body uses the AC sprite cursor (index.html:149). The canvas uses grab/grabbing (:160-161) and the use-targeting reticules (:163-171). OS-level grabs would capture the cursor; film CSS should set cursor:none !important.
Focus: losing focus releases keys (see above). AudioManager mutes and refuses sounds when the page is hidden or unfocused (see 6).
Fullscreen: needs a user gesture. ?fullscreen=1 arms on the first click or keypress (index.html:3286-3299). Do not use fullscreen for film.
Canvas sizing:
 - In preInit3D, agent-mode gives cssW = min(innerWidth, 4096) and cssH = min(innerHeight, 2160); non-agent gives min(innerW-32, 1920) x min(innerH-320, 1080) (scene3d/index.js:881-897).
 - pixelRatio = min(devicePixelRatio, 2) x renderScale (:1245, :1262). renderer.setSize(cssW, cssH, false) (:1288), so drawing buffer = viewport x pixelRatio.
 - ?renderScale in (0, 2] pins the value and disables BOTH the smart initial cap and the adaptive controller (:1235-1262, :1298-1334).
 - Without a pin, computeInitialRenderScale caps the frame near 2.6 Mpx (adaptive_render_scale.js:206-223), so a 3840x2160 viewport starts at about 0.56. The controller can then lower it to 0.35 under load (:1307-1331); ?adaptiveRes=off disables both.
 - Runtime setter: window.__setRenderScale(n) (:1268-1286); it re-reads DPR and resizes the atmosphere pipeline and cloud overlay. Readback: window.__renderScaleState() reports drawingBuffer [w,h] and its source (adaptive_render_scale.js:240-283).
 - The 150 ms-debounced resize handler (:1869-1916) resizes from innerWidth/innerHeight but never re-applies pixelRatio, so call __setRenderScale after changing the device scale factor.
 - Quality order: URL ?quality, then localStorage holtburger_graphics_v1, then a GPU probe, then mid/low (quality.js:956-1052). The GTX 1070 does not match GPU_HIGH_RE (:826), so it defaults to mid unless ?quality=high|ultra is passed.
Exact output size: set the viewport with CDP Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride and pin renderScale.
 - 1080p: 1920x1080, DSF 1, renderScale=1.
 - 4K: 1920x1080 with DSF 2 and renderScale=1. This gives a 3840x2160 buffer whose compositor screenshots are 1:1.
 - 4K alternative: renderScale=2 at DSF 1 also gives a 3840x2160 buffer, but compositor screenshots are downsampled with image-rendering:pixelated. canvas.captureStream records the native buffer either way.
 - There is no API to set a canvas size independent of the window; the resize handler would overwrite a manual setSize on the next resize event.

(6) AUDIO. AudioManager (scene3d/audio/audio_manager.js:147) is built in init3D only when wireframe is off (or ?diag=1) and fetchWave exists (scene3d/index.js:6395-6416). It is exposed as liveScene3d.audioManager.
 - The AudioContext is created only by notifyUserGesture() (:253), hooked to the first window pointerdown/keydown (scene3d/index.js:6410-6416). Before that, play() is a no-op.
 - Graph: BufferSource, then a per-voice Gain, then an HRTF Panner (or the retail stereo-pan nodes), then _effectMaster or _ambientMaster, then _master, then ctx.destination (:387-421, :840-917). There is a 16-voice pool.
 - The listener is set every frame from cameraSwitcher.activeCamera (scene3d/index.js:2551-2562). Ambient gathering is centred on the player (ambient_runtime.js:166).
 - The default "play only when active" setting (:185-196, :294-317) ramps _master to 0 and refuses new sounds whenever document.hidden is true or document.hasFocus() is false. Fix it with ?audioWhenInactive=on or setPlayOnlyWhenActive(false) (:336).
 - Mute: setMasterGain(0) (:443) or pauseAll() (:1046).
 - Capture: dest = am._ctx.createMediaStreamDestination(); am._master.connect(dest). To keep sound off the 1070's speakers, also call am._master.disconnect(am._ctx.destination). Combine dest.stream's audio track with renderer.domElement.captureStream() in a MediaRecorder.

Prior art: capture_canvas_video.cjs (HB root) is an old Playwright script. It used headed Chrome because headless gave a blank software GL context, plus the anti-throttle flags and --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required. It pinned the canvas fixed (an off-screen canvas produced empty frames) and ran a setInterval renderer.render() fallback, which bypasses the composer — do not copy that part.

Note on the user's relayed constraint: nothing here calls an LLM. The film agent is Claude Code (subscription) driving CDP evaluate. The in-page rynth AI director and #hb-thought-overlay (OpenRouter providers, rynth/ai/providers.js) are separate and must stay off: no ?bot=1 and no ?thoughtOverlay.

## APIS
- window.__inputFunnel.poison [ui/input-funnel.js:724]  sig=poison(mode = "throw"|"gate") -> mode :: 'gate' forces the single gameplay gate closed: every keydown stops before raw subscribers and actions (movement, camera C/PageUp/PageDown, hotbar, combat, spellbook, picking Esc). Keyups still reach rawUp subscribers. 'throw' also blocks keyups. Singleton at window.__inputFunnel (getInputFunnel :760-768).
- window.__inputFunnel.unpoison [ui/input-funnel.js:728]  sig=unpoison() -> true :: Re-opens the funnel after a film-mode input lock.
- window.__inputFunnel.releaseHeld [ui/input-funnel.js:567]  sig=releaseHeld(reason: string) -> string[] :: Synthesizes a keyup for every key in the held ledger except Space. This clears the camera keystate, the index gameplay keystate and the cmdInterp edges. Call it before poisoning so nothing stays held (prevents stuck autorun or walking).
- window.__inputFunnel.snapshot / setGate [ui/input-funnel.js:734]  sig=snapshot() -> {v2, installed, gate:{injected, open}, fault, stats, perAction, perRaw}; setGate(fn) at :351 :: Diagnostics, and the gate injection point (index.html:5409 injects enteredWorld && !isTypingInForm()). Calling setGate from outside REPLACES the closure and cannot restore it; use poison/unpoison instead.
- window.__setRenderScale [scene3d/index.js:1268]  sig=(scale: number in (0,2]) -> void :: Sets pixelRatio = min(devicePixelRatio, 2) * scale and calls renderer.setSize(canvas.clientWidth, clientHeight, false), atmospherePipeline.setSize and cloudOverlay.setSize. It is the only path that re-reads DPR after boot. Defined in preInit3D, so it exists before login.
- window.__renderScaleState [scene3d/adaptive_render_scale.js:240]  sig=() -> {renderScale, devicePixelRatio, upscalingFrom, drawingBuffer:[w,h], adaptiveEnabled, settleEnabled, urlPin, source} :: Live readback used to assert the exact output resolution (drawingBuffer is canvas.width x canvas.height). Always installed (:275-283).
- window.__adaptiveRenderScale.stop/start [scene3d/adaptive_render_scale.js:604]  sig=start(); stop(); gpuState() :: The adaptive-resolution controller instance (published at scene3d/index.js:1332). It exists only when no explicit ?renderScale is set, adaptiveRes is on, and neither nullRender nor renderOnDemand is set. stop() freezes the resolution in the middle of a session.
- window.__renderOnce [scene3d/index.js:3007]  sig=() -> boolean :: Advances one tick (sim and render) under ?renderOnDemand=1. dt still comes from the wall clock (performance.now), clamped to 0.1 s. Under the default-on syncPhysicsTick it returns BEFORE the frame completes.
- AudioManager (liveScene3d.audioManager) [scene3d/audio/audio_manager.js:147]  sig=notifyUserGesture() :253; resume() :428; setMasterGain(v) :443; setEffectGain/setAmbientGain; setPlayOnlyWhenActive(on) :336; setActive(b) :260; setListener(posThree, quatThree) :514; play(did, worldPos, opts) :710; playFromCenter(did, vol, opts) :769; pauseAll() :1046 :: The game's only WebAudio graph. Private nodes _ctx, _master (to ctx.destination), _effectMaster and _ambientMaster (to _master) are created by _initContext at :387-421 only after notifyUserGesture. Constructed at scene3d/index.js:6397 and assigned to liveScene3d.audioManager at :6403.
- EntityManager.showSpeechBubble [scene3d/entities.js:7154]  sig=showSpeechBubble(guid, text, isEmote) :: The only entry point for overhead speech/emote sprites. Called from app/client_events.js:1583-1592, which checks typeof === 'function' on every event, so swapping in a no-op instance method suppresses bubbles at runtime.
- showSpeechBubbleOnEntity / removeSpeechBubbleFromEntity [scene3d/speech_bubble.js:171]  sig=showSpeechBubbleOnEntity(inst, text, isEmote) -> Sprite|null; removeSpeechBubbleFromEntity(inst) at :237 :: Bakes and attaches the bubble sprite (renderOrder 11, 3.05 m above the rig, 4.5 s hold plus 1.2 s fade). removeSpeechBubbleFromEntity purges a live bubble; iterate entityManager.entityMap to clear all of them.
- SelectionBracketLayer.setDisplayOn / setTarget [scene3d/selection_brackets.js:898]  sig=setDisplayOn(on: boolean); setTarget(guid, follow, sphere) at :873 :: Hides or shows the retail corner brackets and the off-screen arrow. The setting stays put: the CharacterOption 0x0E poll only re-applies on an option change (:910-920). Available as liveScene3d.selectionBracketLayer, or null under ?hud=none or ?selectionIndicator=none.
- EntityManager.setSelectedTarget / getSelectedTarget [scene3d/entities.js:8748]  sig=setSelectedTarget(guid) ; guid 0 clears :: Clears the selection, which removes the brackets, the legacy torus and the range check. Film mode should call setSelectedTarget(0) when it starts.
- EntityManager.setLocalPlayerCameraOpacity [scene3d/entities.js:18991]  sig=setLocalPlayerCameraOpacity(guid, opacity 0..1) :: Applies a hierarchical camera fade (body plus held children, re-applied across re-dress and respawn) to the local rig. Opacity 0 hides the camera-operator avatar. The guid comes from window.getLocalPlayerGuid().
- EntityManager.setVisibility [scene3d/entities.js:7092]  sig=setVisibility(guid, visible) :: Sets state-authoritative rig visibility (normally driven by kind=17). It also calls noteEntityVisibility, which can play Hidden/UnHide scripts for genuine HIDDEN bits. A server SetState can flip it back.
- portal_space exports [scene3d/portal_space.js:1434]  sig=startPortalSpace(scene3d, opts) :1434; signalPortalArrived({cellId}) :1578; isPortalSpaceActive() :1589; portalSpaceOwnsFrame() :1597; endPortalSpace() :1826; destinationCellsReady(scene3d, cellId) :601; destinationBuildInFlight(scene3d, cellId) :617 :: The teleport tunnel state machine. globalThis.__isPortalSpaceActive is installed at :1594 and window.__portalSpace diagnostics are published at :1170-1199. Importable with import('./scene3d/portal_space.js'), the same module instance that client_events uses.
- window.__cam (camDebug free camera) [scene3d/camera.js:1484]  sig=park(); release(); parked; set(ex,ey,ez,tx,ty,tz); orbit(tx,ty,tz,dist,azDeg,elDeg); player(dist,azDeg,elDeg,dz); fov(v); info(); world() :: Installed only with ?camDebug=on (:463-473). park() suspends positionCamera so the active camera keeps a pose set by a script. Coordinates are AC world metres. set() uses cam.up=(0,1,0) plus lookAt (:1496-1497), which breaks down at +/-90 degree pitch.
- CameraSwitcher [scene3d/camera.js:408]  sig=switchMode(next) :891; tick(dt) :1179; activeCamera (prop); keys {w,a,s,d,q,e,shift}; _endFollowDrag(); getActive() :1137; dispose() :3294 :: Owns follow/topDown/orbit, the per-mode DOM listeners (_listeners) and the global ones (_globalListeners / _funnelUnbinds). activeCamera is what the frame renders, what the audio listener follows and what the brackets project through.
- boot readiness globals [index.html:4265]  sig=window.__bootState; window.__bootStateHistory[]; window.__sceneReadyEverFired; window.__setBootState(state,msg); event 'holtburger:state' :: States run init, connecting, in-world, ready. 'ready' fires after the atmosphere pipeline and the first shader prewarm (scene3d/index.js:6289-6292). __sceneReadyEverFired stays latched even if 'in-world' overwrites the scalar.
- plugin event bus portalSpaceEntered/Exited [app/client_events.js:882]  sig=window.__pluginClient.events.on('portalSpaceEntered'|'portalSpaceExited', fn) :: Entered fires on kind=33 even with ?portalSpace=off. Exited fires only through the tunnel's onExit (:934-936). __pluginClient exists even under ?plugins=none.
- renderer / capture canvas [scene3d/index.js:1159]  sig=new THREE.WebGLRenderer({canvas, antialias, logarithmicDepthBuffer:true}) :: liveScene3d.renderer.domElement is #canvas. It has no preserveDrawingBuffer, and alpha uses the three r184 default of false (node_modules/three/src/renderers/WebGLRenderer.js:77). Composer path at :2764-2797, direct path at :2799-2984.
- canvas.captureStream / MediaRecorder output size [capture_canvas_video.cjs:245] (UNVERIFIED) sig=canvas.captureStream(fps) -> MediaStream :: Prior art: records the canvas drawing buffer, so resolution equals canvas.width x canvas.height. That this is browser behaviour, not repo code, is NOT verified here.

## SEAMS
- [index.html:484] Boot-time agent-mode and no-hud classes, with their CSS (index.html:604-619 toggle; :456-525 agent rules; :536-539 no-hud rules). The canvas-size branch _isAgentMode is latched in preInit3D (scene3d/index.js:881-887) and passed to the resize handler (:1872-1873). => Launch film sessions with ?agent=1 (or ?autoLogin=1) at load; adding the class later does not resize the canvas. Use ?hud=none at load, or classList.add('no-hud') at runtime, to hide all hb-* HUD. Add a film-mode class with CSS such as `html.film-mode body #canvas{border:0!important;cursor:none!important;image-rendering:auto!important}` and `html.film-mode, html.film-mode *{cursor:none!important}`. Brackets need specificity above (2 ids, 1 class, 2 elements) or setDisplayOn(false).
- [app/client_events.js:1568] Speech-bubble dispatch: the kind=55 handler calls window.liveScene3d.entityManager.showSpeechBubble, which is looked up on every event. => Film start: save the method, replace it with a no-op, and remove live bubbles (removeSpeechBubbleFromEntity, or set inst._speechBubble.visible=false over entityMap). Film end: restore the method. Optionally keep bubbles for dialogue shots.
- [scene3d/selection_brackets.js:898] Selection indicator: SelectionBracketLayer.setDisplayOn and EntityManager.setSelectedTarget. => setSelectedTarget(0) plus selectionBracketLayer?.setDisplayOn(false) during film; reverse afterwards. Brackets also auto-appear when auto-targeting in melee/missile mode (index.html:4679-4689).
- [ui/input-funnel.js:724] Input funnel singleton window.__inputFunnel: one gate, poison/unpoison, releaseHeld. => Reversible keyboard lock: releaseHeld('film') then poison('gate'); undo with unpoison(). Covers movement, the camera C/PageUp/PageDown keys, hotbar, combat, spellbook and picking Esc.
- [scene3d/camera.js:1067] Window capture phase is the earliest dispatch point for any listener registered after page boot. The funnel listens at document capture; the camera, picking, OrbitControls and hover tooltip listen on the canvas or document. => Register window capture blockers that call stopImmediatePropagation and preventDefault for key*, pointer*, mouse*, click, dblclick, auxclick, contextmenu, wheel (passive:false), touch*, dragstart and drop. Also call cameraSwitcher._endFollowDrag?.() and zero cameraSwitcher.keys. Remove the blockers on exit. A DOM shield div does not work because agent-mode and no-hud CSS hide it.
- [scene3d/index.js:1268] Render resolution controls: window.__setRenderScale, window.__renderScaleState, window.__adaptiveRenderScale, the ?renderScale and ?adaptiveRes URL pins, and the debounced resize handler. => Before recording: set the CDP viewport and DSF, call __setRenderScale(n) to re-read DPR, assert __renderScaleState().drawingBuffer equals the target and source is 'url', and call __adaptiveRenderScale?.stop() if it exists.
- [scene3d/index.js:2722] cameraSwitcher.activeCamera is the single camera read by the render (scene3d/index.js:2722), the audio listener (:2552), the bracket projection (loop.js:3451) and the portal FOV fade (portal_space.js:1132). => Drive the film camera through activeCamera, or through __cam.park plus writing the persp camera's position and quaternion directly. Render, spatial audio and overlays then stay consistent. A camera kept outside activeCamera would leave the audio listener on the player camera.
- [scene3d/index.js:572] Per-frame render exits all call recordRenderDiag(renderer, scene): composer at :2784, direct path at :2966, portal at :2739. There is no public post-render hook. => Add a film hook (for example window.__filmOnFrame?.()) next to recordRenderDiag so it calls videoTrack.requestFrame() on canvas.captureStream(0), giving exactly one captured frame per rendered frame. Or wrap liveScene3d.atmospherePipeline.render (assigned at :5926) without a source edit.
- [scene3d/portal_space.js:1170] Portal-space controls. Diagnostics: window.__portalSpace, globalThis.__isPortalSpaceActive. Bus events portalSpaceEntered/Exited. Exports endPortalSpace, destinationCellsReady, destinationBuildInFlight. The ?portalSpace, ?portalSound and ?portalDrone URL params are re-read per event or per start. => Option A: keep the tunnel on and MediaRecorder.pause() while __isPortalSpaceActive() is true; resume about 1.5 s after it turns false, which clears the exit whoosh, plus a settle on frame time. Option B: history.replaceState to add portalSpace=off, then gate on kind=66 plus destinationCellsReady && !destinationBuildInFlight && !__interiorBuildPending plus N stable frames.
- [scene3d/audio/audio_manager.js:387] Audio graph tap through the private AudioManager fields _ctx and _master, plus setPlayOnlyWhenActive. => Sequence: am.setPlayOnlyWhenActive(false); am.notifyUserGesture(); await am.resume(); create dest with am._ctx.createMediaStreamDestination(); am._master.connect(dest). On the 1070 also am._master.disconnect(am._ctx.destination). Record new MediaStream([canvasTrack, ...dest.stream.getAudioTracks()]).
- [scene3d/entities.js:18991] Local player rig visibility: setLocalPlayerCameraOpacity(guid, o), setVisibility(guid, v), and window.getLocalPlayerGuid. => Hide the camera-operator avatar (and its held items) during b-roll shots; restore to 1 or true afterwards. Prefer the opacity path, which is client-only. Confirm separately whether the faded rig still casts a shadow.
- [scene3d/index.js:6289] Scene readiness: __sceneReadyEverFired / __bootState==='ready' (index.html:4275), liveScene3d.atmospherePipeline non-null (scene3d/index.js:5926), liveScene3d.cloudOverlay (:5700, only with ?clouds=on). => Wait for all of these before the first take. Until the pipeline exists, frames take the direct path and look different (no aerial perspective, bloom or tone curve).
- [scene3d/camera.js:1457] ?camDebug=on free-camera rig, window.__cam. => A ready-made way to take over the camera (park, set, orbit, fov). Write quaternions directly rather than calling set() to avoid the lookAt singularity at straight-down tilts.

## HAZARDS
- [index.html:484] ?agent=1 is not clean: the kill rule allowlists every id^='hb-' body child plus .hb-bar/.hb-pill/.hb-panel. All gameplay HUDs, toasts, #hb-portal-space-notice, #hb-jump-charge and #hb-thought-overlay therefore stay visible, and #selection-brackets-3d is forced visible. || mitig: Use ?agent=1&hud=none (optionally &plugins=none) at load, or classList.add('no-hud') at runtime, plus selectionBracketLayer.setDisplayOn(false).
- [scene3d/speech_bubble.js:171] Speech/emote bubbles are in-canvas THREE.Sprites with no URL flag (?speechBubbles was removed). Neither hud=none nor agent-mode hides them. || mitig: Replace entityManager.showSpeechBubble with a no-op during film and purge live bubbles.
- [index.html:160] The canvas keeps `border:1px solid #ccc; image-rendering:pixelated; cursor:grab` from `#stage canvas` in agent-mode, because the agent #canvas rule (:497-501) never resets border. Expect a 1px line on the top and left edges of compositor screenshots (reasoned from the CSS, not observed). Supersampled buffers are downscaled nearest-neighbour. || mitig: Film CSS: border:0, image-rendering:auto and cursor:none with !important on #canvas. Prefer canvas.captureStream, which records the raw buffer.
- [scene3d/index.js:881] The canvas-size mode (_isAgentMode) is latched once in preInit3D. Non-agent pages cap the canvas at 1920x1080 CSS minus 32/320 px of page chrome; agent pages cap it at 4096x2160. || mitig: Load the page with ?agent=1 or ?autoLogin=1; a runtime class toggle will not fix sizing.
- [scene3d/adaptive_render_scale.js:206] Without an explicit ?renderScale, the smart default caps the initial frame near 2.6 Mpx (a 4K viewport starts at about 0.56). The adaptive controller can then drop to 0.35 in the middle of a recording, changing resolution between frames. || mitig: Always pass ?renderScale=1 (or 2), or ?adaptiveRes=off. Verify with __renderScaleState().source==='url' and the drawingBuffer size.
- [scene3d/index.js:1869] The resize handler never re-applies pixelRatio, so a CDP DPR or DSF change after boot leaves a stale pixel ratio. || mitig: Call window.__setRenderScale(n) after any viewport or DSF change, then re-check __renderScaleState().
- [scene3d/portal_space.js:113] Every teleport, including admin @teleloc/@tele, plays the portal tunnel (the world is not drawn). It lasts arrival plus load plus about 4-7 s: CONTINUE 2-5 s, 1 s fade-out, 1 s black fade-in. Enter, drone and exit sounds play, and the loop is paced to 30 fps. Agent-mode skips only the LOGIN tunnel. || mitig: Pause the recorder while __isPortalSpaceActive() is true and resume after a settle, or set ?portalSpace=off and gate on the readiness checks.
- [app/client_events.js:912] With ?portalSpace=off the camera jumps instantly, terrain/EnvCells/entities pop in on screen, and program warm-up (which only runs while the tunnel owns the frame) can cause hitches in the first frames. || mitig: Do not record from the teleport command until destinationCellsReady && !destinationBuildInFlight && !__interiorBuildPending hold, plus about 1-2 s of stable frame times.
- [scene3d/index.js:2501] After a frame gap over 0.5 s, the sim freezes for 10 frames (dt=0). Shader-link stalls therefore produce visible micro-freezes in footage. || mitig: Pre-warm by holding the camera on the shot for a few seconds before recording, and discard takes whose frame-time log shows gaps.
- [scene3d/audio/audio_manager.js:194] AudioContext does not exist until notifyUserGesture(); play() is a no-op before it. The default 'play only when active' mutes _master and refuses new sounds whenever the tab is hidden or unfocused, which is likely in headless or off-screen Chrome. || mitig: Use ?audioWhenInactive=on or setPlayOnlyWhenActive(false), call notifyUserGesture() then resume(), and launch Chrome with --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required.
- [scene3d/audio/audio_manager.js:398] On the 1070 a person uses the machine, and no sound may reach them. A default graph plays into ctx.destination, even from a headless or off-screen tab. || mitig: Call am._master.disconnect(am._ctx.destination) and record only through a MediaStreamDestination. Also launch Chrome with --mute-audio after checking that capture still receives samples.
- [scene3d/index.js:948] ?wireframe=1 (without ?diag=1) never constructs AudioManager and skips the atmosphere, clouds, sky and CSM. || mitig: Never use wireframe for film; the laptop's SwiftShader cannot produce film output, so real-GPU takes run on the 1070.
- [scene3d/audio/ambient_runtime.js:166] The audio listener follows the active camera, but ambient sound gathering is centred on the player. A drone shot far from the avatar hears the player's ambience, attenuated and panned from far away. || mitig: Either keep the avatar near the shot (teleport it), or record game audio separately or replace it with the music track.
- [scene3d/quality.js:924] Persisted localStorage prefs change the look and sound on a reused Chrome profile: holtburger_graphics_v1 (quality preset and flags), holtburger_camera_v1 (stiffness, FOV, distance, autofollow), hb.options.audio.v1 (gains, play-only-when-active). || mitig: Use a dedicated --user-data-dir for film and pass explicit URL flags (?quality=ultra etc.).
- [scene3d/quality.js:826] The GTX 1070 is not matched by GPU_HIGH_RE, so the auto preset resolves to 'mid'. || mitig: Pass ?quality=high or ?quality=ultra explicitly.
- [scene3d/picking.js:1451] Mouse input is outside the keyboard funnel: right-drag mouselook, the wheel, OrbitControls, picking clicks (a double-click can Use a portal or door) and the hover tooltip. F-key panel hotkeys are also outside it. || mitig: Install window capture-phase blockers for all pointer, mouse, wheel and key events in addition to poison('gate').
- [scene3d/camera.js:1496] Follow-mode pitch is clamped to [-0.5, 1.4] rad, and __cam.set uses up=(0,1,0) plus lookAt, which is degenerate at +/-90 degree pitch. A straight-down tilt flips or jitters. || mitig: Film camera: build orientation from quaternions (slerp or swing-twist) and write camera.quaternion directly; never lookAt at the poles.
- [app/dom_utils.js:24] The disconnect banner id hbDisconnectBanner has no hyphen, so agent-mode hides it and a dead session looks normal in footage. || mitig: Watch __bootState / kind=4 DISCONNECTED in the film controller and abort the take.
- [capture_canvas_video.cjs:57] The old capture script found that headless Chrome on Windows gave a blank software GL context, an off-screen canvas gave empty captureStream frames, and its setInterval renderer.render() fallback bypassed the composer (wrong look). || mitig: Use the runbook's 1070 off-screen CDP Chrome with a real GPU, keep agent-mode so the canvas fills the viewport, add the anti-throttle flags, and never call renderer.render directly.
- [scene3d/index.js:1603] A 2 m orange MeshStandard 'hello-cube' sits permanently at AC world (0,0,5) under worldRoot. || mitig: Set liveScene3d.helloCube.visible=false in film mode; it only matters near landblock 0x0000.
- [scene3d/index.js:3002] __renderOnce returns before the frame completes under the default-on syncPhysicsTick, and dt is wall-clock. Offline fixed-timestep rendering is not supported, and the server-driven world keeps moving in real time. || mitig: Capture in real time at a sustainable resolution and quality; use renderOnDemand only for stills.
- [index-bundled.html:1022] The player proxy (:7080/tunnel) can serve the bundled shell (index-bundled.html plus shell/app-<hash>.js). serve.py (:8765) always serves live sources. || mitig: Drive film sessions through serve.py with ?nosw=1, or check the x-hb-shell response header.

## RECS
- Base film URL: ?autoLogin=1&account=..&password=..&autoSpawn=first&agent=1&hud=none&plugins=none&selectionIndicator=none&quality=ultra&renderScale=1&audioWhenInactive=on&nosw=1&camDebug=on. Nameplates are already off by default; nameplates=on and nameplateDom=on must be absent. Do not pass bot or thoughtOverlay. Keep portalSpace on and cut around teleports; replaceState can toggle it at runtime.
- Chrome launch flags, from capture_canvas_video.cjs prior art: --disable-background-timer-throttling --disable-renderer-backgrounding --disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows --disable-features=CalculateNativeWinOcclusion --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required, plus --mute-audio and a dedicated --user-data-dir on the 1070.
- Exact resolution: CDP Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride gives the viewport. 1080p is 1920x1080, DSF 1, renderScale=1. 4K is 1920x1080, DSF 2, renderScale=1 (the buffer then matches compositor screenshots), or renderScale=2 at DSF 1 for captureStream only. After the override call window.__setRenderScale(n), then assert __renderScaleState().drawingBuffer and source==='url'.
- Film-mode enter, in order:
1. releaseHeld('film'), then __inputFunnel.poison('gate').
2. Install the window capture-phase input blockers.
3. cameraSwitcher._endFollowDrag?.(), and clear autorun (window.__autoRunOn) and the camera keys.
4. Add the no-hud and film-mode classes (border, cursor and image-rendering fixes).
5. entityManager.setSelectedTarget(0) and selectionBracketLayer?.setDisplayOn(false).
6. Patch showSpeechBubble and purge existing bubbles.
7. Optionally setLocalPlayerCameraOpacity(localGuid, 0) and helloCube.visible=false.
Exit reverses every step. Keep the saved originals in a closure.
- Capture: renderer.domElement.captureStream(0) with videoTrack.requestFrame() called from a new post-render hook beside recordRenderDiag at scene3d/index.js:2739/2784/2966, which gives one captured frame per rendered frame. Fallback: captureStream(fps). Mux the AudioManager MediaStreamDestination track into the same MediaRecorder. Stream chunks out via CDP rather than one huge blob download.
- Gate the first take on __sceneReadyEverFired, liveScene3d.atmospherePipeline, an idle streaming backlog and a few seconds of stable frame times. Gate each take after a teleport on __portalSpace.state===0, plus a settle of at least 1.5 s so the exit whoosh is not recorded, plus stable frame times. Abort on __bootState==='error' or kind=4.
- Implement a new film-mode module as a default-off ?filmMode=on opt-in exposing window.__film {enter(), exit(), setResolution(), shield on/off, audioTap()}. Keep all hiding reversible and runtime-only, so normal play is byte-identical when the flag is off. Under the repo's default-on-no-eyetest-gate rule it becomes a candidate to flip on once validated.
- For 90-degree tilts and corridor turns, the film camera must own orientation as a quaternion (slerp or squad between keyframes) and write activeCamera.quaternion directly. Never route through camera.js lookAt with up=(0,1,0), and never route through follow mode (its pitch is clamped to 1.4 rad).

## OPENQ
- Does the 1070's off-screen or headless Chrome (CDP :9333) get a real-GPU WebGL context today? capture_canvas_video.cjs recorded a blank software context in headless on Windows. The answer decides headless-new vs headed-off-screen for film.
- Does Chrome --mute-audio also silence MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode capture, or only device output? Disconnecting _master from ctx.destination is the code-level guarantee either way.
- Does document.hasFocus() return true in the chosen headless or off-screen mode? If not, does CDP Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled(true) keep AudioManager active? (?audioWhenInactive=on sidesteps this.)
- Timing of requestFrame() on a captureStream(0) track relative to the cloud overlay and portal fade quad, which draw AFTER composer.render (scene3d/index.js:2779-2783): does the captured frame always include the final overlay draws?
- Real-time headroom on the GTX 1070 at 4K ultra (composer, clouds, CSM) plus MediaRecorder encoding: can it hold 30 or 60 fps, or should 4K be produced by upscaling 1440p/1080p captures?
- Does postprocessing's atmospherePipeline.setSize(cssW, cssH) allocate composer buffers at CSS size times renderer.getPixelRatio()? Not read; affects 4K sharpness under renderScale=2.
- Does setLocalPlayerCameraOpacity(guid, 0) also remove the avatar's shadow (CSM caster) and attached particle emitters? Should the film module hide the rig through setVisibility instead (risk of a server SetState override)?
- Should film footage ever include speech bubbles for in-world dialogue scenes? If so, it needs a styled, filmable variant instead of the gameplay sprite.
